subject: Dedicated capacity demo request — latency & throughput details
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@orbitai.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-21T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Demo — Dedicated capacity for inference (throughput/latency)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks — I just signed up and flagged Orbit AI as a warm lead through the self-serve flow. We're evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing feature that will need predictable low-latency inference at fairly high throughput. Would love to set up a dedicated-capacity demo focused on:

- P50/P95 latency under sustained load
- Sustained QPS and concurrent request handling
- Autoscale / burst behavior and SLAs
- Cost/throughput tradeoffs (quantization, batching, cache)

Quick context: our service ingests short user prompts (~60 tokens) and needs P50 < 300ms, target P95 < 750ms at ~3,000 concurrent active sessions during peak. Peak QPS is in the range of ~2k–4k. We'll need to understand what Dedicated pools look like and how to size for that workload.

I've attached a small telemetry sample and an internal capacity spreadsheet to help with sizing (orbit-capacity-telemetry.csv). Can you put together 30–45 minutes for a walkthrough this week?

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering — Orbit AI
samira@orbitai.com

[attachment: orbit-capacity-telemetry.csv]

2) Are requests single-turn short prompts exclusively (~60 tokens), or do you have multi-turn flows with cacheable prefixes?

Suggested times (PDT):
- Thu Jun 24 — 10:00–10:45 AM
- Thu Jun 24 — 3:00–3:45 PM
- Fri Jun 25 — 11:00–11:45 AM

I’ve attached a short demo agenda and a small checklist we use for Dedicated intake (rdw_demo_agenda.docx). Ben (SDR) and Irene (Solutions Eng) will join — Irene can drive the latency/throughput sizing.

If any of those slots work, I’ll send a calendar invite with a quick runbook and a short pre-call questionnaire.

Best,

Hi Samira — I’m Ben, nice to meet you. Thanks for the telemetry — that helps a lot. Quick question on the live-test idea: do you have a staging endpoint we can hit during the demo, or would you prefer we run a synthetic generator from our side against a sandbox model? Both are possible but the routing and network path changes the latency profile, so we want to set expectations.

If you don’t have staging, we normally run a synthetic load against an identical model pinned to a dedicated pool to show P50/P95 behavior. If you do have staging and want realistic network characteristics, we’ll need:
- an allowed IP range (or temporary token) to hit your staging endpoint, and
- a contact who can watch logs on your side when we run the test.

Proposed slot: Thu Jun 24 — 3:00–3:45 PM (Irene confirmed availability). I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Also attaching our Dedicated intake checklist so we can capture the fine-grain sizing items before the call (capacity-checklist.pdf).
